title: Averaging earlier CalCOFI water types creates a positive lower bound on added oxygen use in a four-property mixture test
abstract: We tested whether salinity, nitrate, phosphate and oxygen on sigma0 26.5 require added oxygen use to fit the 2007-2020 CalCOFI mean. We used final bottle data and equal weights for 225 common station-season cells. Mean oxygen fell by 22.48 umol/kg from 1984-1995. Linear programs fit the later four-property mean with any mixture of earlier local water types and an added reaction at O:N:P = -170:16:1. Earlier types averaged within one year permit 0-45.00 umol/kg of added oxygen use. Averaging the same earlier observations over 12 years gives 8.11-11.32. Averaging shrinks the mixture set and can thus introduce a positive reaction bound. The zero minimum survives removal of extreme casts and deletion of each earlier year. All 500 resampled late-year targets fit the one-year model with zero added use; only 302 fit the 12-year reaction model. Independent full-column programs confirm the primary minima. These bounds are conditional on a permissive local source library. They do not establish actual transport or separate water age from respiration rate. They show why a narrow reaction range from averaged source types is not a robust attribution. Final-data input, code, numerical witnesses, uncertainty tests and provenance are included.

display.caption: Averaging the earlier water types narrows the allowed mixture set and changes the minimum added oxygen use from zero to 8.11 umol/kg. These are conditional bounds, not estimates of a physical respiration share.
